config.title: align-items and align-content

intro.title: align-items and align-content
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout using flexbox to arrange colored boxes within a container. You will learn the core CSS concepts of align-items and align-content, which control how flex items are positioned along the cross axis. The main technologies involved are CSS Flexbox properties, specifically align-items for aligning individual items and align-content for aligning multiple lines of items. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand the difference between these two properties and how to apply them to create organized, visually appealing layouts.
intro.usecase: The align-items and align-content properties are essential for creating professional layouts in modern web applications. You'll use them to vertically align navigation items in headers, position form labels and inputs consistently, and organize dashboard widgets into clean grids. These properties ensure UI elements maintain proper spacing and alignment across different screen sizes, which is critical for user-friendly interfaces like admin panels, e-commerce product listings, and social media feeds.

objectives: Apply the align-items property to vertically position flex items within a container
Configure the align-content property to control spacing between multiple flex lines
Construct flexbox layouts that demonstrate the difference between align-items and align-content
Manipulate flex container properties to achieve specific vertical alignment patterns
Implement responsive designs using appropriate alignment properties for different screen sizes
Integrate alignment properties with other flexbox features to create complex layouts
Control vertical spacing in multi-line flex containers using alignment properties

steps.title: Create a flex container with multiple rows
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named .container that sets display to flex and flex-wrap to wrap.
steps.hint: Use the .container selector and set display: flex; and flex-wrap: wrap; inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container class is created with display: flex and flex-wrap: wrap properties to enable a flex container that can wrap items to multiple rows.
successCriteria: The .container class exists with both display: flex and flex-wrap: wrap properties correctly set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included both display: flex and flex-wrap: wrap properties in the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container class should have display: flex and flex-wrap: wrap properties to create a proper flex container with wrapping.

steps.title: Style the container with fixed dimensions
steps.instruction: Add height: 400px and width: 600px to the .container class to create a visible boundary.
steps.hint: Add the height and width properties inside the .container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container class will have fixed dimensions, creating a constrained visual space for the flex items.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes height: 400px and width: 600px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both height: 400px and width: 600px to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container still needs fixed dimensions. Add height: 400px and width: 600px to the .container class.

steps.title: Add border to visualize container boundaries
steps.instruction: Add a 2px solid border with color #333 to the .container class to make its boundaries clearly visible.
steps.hint: Use the border property with the values: 2px solid #333.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a visible dark gray border around it, making its edges easy to see.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a border, but check if it's exactly 2px solid #333.
steps.feedbackWrong: The border property is missing or incorrect. Add border: 2px solid #333; to the .container class.

steps.title: Create flex items with consistent styling
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named .item with the following properties: padding: 20px, background-color: lightblue, border: 2px solid darkblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule starting with .item { } and include each property inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS class named .item is created with the specified styling properties for uniform flex items.
successCriteria: The .item class exists with padding: 20px, background-color: lightblue, border: 2px solid darkblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .item class, but some properties are missing or incorrect. Check that you have padding: 20px, background-color: lightblue, border: 2px solid darkblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item class is not correctly defined. Make sure to create a CSS rule for .item with the specified properties.

steps.title: Add varying heights to flex items
steps.instruction: Add different height values to individual .item classes using nth-child selectors to create visual distinction between items.
steps.hint: Use the selector .item:nth-child(n) to target specific items and set different height values (e.g., 60px, 80px, 100px).
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will have different heights, creating visual distinction between rows when flex-wrap creates multiple lines.
successCriteria: At least three .item:nth-child selectors with different height values are added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some height variations, but try to add at least three different height values using .item:nth-child selectors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding different height values to individual flex items using nth-child selectors. Check if you've used the correct selector syntax and specified height values.

steps.title: Apply align-items: center to the container
steps.instruction: Add the align-items property with value center to the .container class to center items vertically within each row.
steps.hint: Add the property inside the .container selector. The value should be center.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will be centered vertically within each row, while maintaining their horizontal layout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added align-items: center inside the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-items property with value center is missing from the .container class. Try adding it now.

steps.title: Observe align-items effect on single rows
steps.instruction: Add the align-items: center property to the .container selector to see how it vertically centers items within each row.
steps.hint: Look for the .container selector in your CSS and add the align-items property with the value center.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will be vertically centered within their respective rows, making the effect of align-items visible.
successCriteria: The .container selector includes the align-items: center property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added align-items: center to the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the align-items property with the value center to the .container selector.

steps.title: Change align-items to flex-start
steps.instruction: In the .container selector, change the align-items value from 'center' to 'flex-start'.
steps.hint: Look for the align-items property in the .container rule and replace its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will align to the top (start) of each row instead of being centered vertically.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the align-items property value in the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-items property in .container should be set to flex-start.

steps.title: Apply align-content: space-between to the container
steps.instruction: Add the align-content property with value space-between to your existing .container class to distribute the flex rows with equal space between them.
steps.hint: Add a new line inside the .container rule: align-content: space-between;
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex rows will be spaced apart with equal gaps between them, while items within each row remain centered vertically.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added align-content: space-between; inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-content property wasn't added correctly. Add align-content: space-between; to the .container class.

steps.title: Observe combined effect of align-items and align-content
steps.instruction: Observe how the flex items are now aligned both within each row (center due to align-items) and with spacing between rows (space-between due to align-content).
steps.hint: Look at the visual result: items are centered vertically within their rows, and rows are evenly spaced apart within the container height.
steps.analogousExample: /* Visual observation: align-items controls vertical alignment within each row, align-content controls spacing between rows */
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see the combined effect: items centered vertically within their rows, with equal spacing between rows filling the container height.
successCriteria: The CSS includes both align-items: center and align-content: space-between properties, and the visual result demonstrates their combined effect.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're observing both properties working together: align-items centers items within rows, align-content spaces rows apart.
steps.feedbackWrong: The observation isn't complete. Look at how align-items controls vertical alignment within each row while align-content controls spacing between rows.
